scope: Provider capabilities for Active integrations. AMLOK schedules are deployment-specific.

integrations.cadence: On supported events; API reads for reconciliation.
integrations.method: Stripe emits webhooks when supported payment, refund, dispute, and payout events occur. API reads retrieve the corresponding resources; there is no single recurring refresh interval for all payment data.
integrations.conditions: Event delivery can be delayed, duplicated, or out of order. Settlement and funds availability follow the payment lifecycle, so an event does not imply funds have settled.

integrations.cadence: Event notifications typically within 60 seconds.
integrations.method: Square typically sends webhook notifications within 60 seconds of a supported event. Authorized API reads can retrieve the associated payment, order, inventory, or other supported resource.
integrations.conditions: This is Square's typical notification timing, not an AMLOK end-to-end delivery guarantee. Failed deliveries may be retried for up to 24 hours; event subscriptions require the relevant permissions.

integrations.cadence: After supported card-transaction events.
integrations.method: Helcim sends a webhook after a supported card transaction is processed. The notification identifies the transaction; the Card Transaction API supplies its full details.
integrations.conditions: Webhooks must be enabled for the required events. Delivery retries can delay updates. The card-transaction event does not establish a recurring refresh interval for every Helcim resource.

integrations.cadence: Near-real-time notifications for subscribed topics.
integrations.method: Shopify provides near-real-time webhooks for subscribed topics such as orders, refunds, and inventory changes. Its APIs support follow-up retrieval and periodic reconciliation.
integrations.conditions: Shopify does not guarantee webhook delivery or ordering. Reconciliation is needed for missed events; available topics, protected data access, and API throttling depend on the app and shop.

integrations.cadence: On supported changes; delivery depends on the store.
integrations.method: WooCommerce supports webhooks for changes to orders, products, customers, and coupons. Notifications are delivered through the store's background processing; API reads can reconcile supported resources.
integrations.conditions: Store hosting, background jobs, plugins, and webhook health affect delivery time. Webhooks can be disabled after repeated failures. There is no universal minute-based refresh promise across WooCommerce stores.

integrations.cadence: On supported order, listing, and inventory events.
integrations.method: Etsy provides webhooks for supported order, listing, and inventory events. Subscribed events can prompt retrieval of the relevant authorized API resources.
integrations.conditions: Event coverage is specific: an inventory event is not a notification for every possible stock change. App authorization, scopes, and the supported event list determine coverage. Other data requires scheduled API reads within the app's limits.

integrations.cadence: On supported entity changes; CDC for reconciliation.
integrations.method: QuickBooks Online supports entity-change webhooks and Change Data Capture (CDC). Intuit recommends CDC reconciliation after missed events and suggests a daily CDC call for required entities.
integrations.conditions: The daily CDC check is an Intuit integration recommendation, not a statement that all data updates only daily. Notifications can be delayed or out of sequence; coverage depends on the entities and permissions enabled.

integrations.cadence: At the configured Web Connector interval or manual run.
integrations.method: QuickBooks Desktop Web Connector initiates scheduled or manual exchanges with the authorized company file. Its normal user interface supports update intervals of one minute or longer; the service can enforce a higher minimum.
integrations.conditions: The connector must be running and able to access the company file. A configured interval is the minimum time between connections, not a completion guarantee. Confirm compatibility with the installed Canadian edition.

integrations.cadence: On supported webhook events; API reads for other data.
integrations.method: Xero supports app-level webhook subscriptions for supported event categories across connected organizations. The applicable API supplies the resources needed after a notification or during a scheduled read.
integrations.conditions: Webhook coverage does not include every accounting resource. Retry or disabled subscriptions can delay delivery, and API access and limits govern reconciliation. Confirm the categories used by your connected organization.

integrations.cadence: On supported accounting events.
integrations.method: FreshBooks sends callbacks for subscribed events, including supported invoice, payment, expense, and client changes made through its application or API. These events can prompt an authorized resource read.
integrations.conditions: The webhook must be verified and have the required scopes. Supported events do not define a fixed refresh interval for every report or accounting resource; remaining reads follow the configured schedule.

integrations.cadence: On supported invoice, estimate, and checkout events.
integrations.method: Wave supports webhooks for selected invoice, estimate, and checkout events. Receiving webhooks requires an authorized Pro account and the appropriate OAuth scopes.
integrations.conditions: These notifications do not represent every ledger or bank-feed change. Other accessible resources require API retrieval on the configured schedule. Missing scopes prevent delivery for the affected business.

sources.title: Wave webhook setup and event coverage

integrations.cadence: When configured workflow rules trigger.
integrations.method: Zoho Books supports outgoing webhooks associated with workflow rules. Matching events can notify the integration; authorized API reads retrieve supported records and reconcile changes.
integrations.conditions: The organization's enabled modules, workflow criteria, permissions, and API limits determine coverage and timing. Workflow notifications are not a universal change feed for every accounting record.

integrations.cadence: When event-based or scheduled workflow rules trigger.
integrations.method: Zoho Inventory supports workflow webhooks with immediate or time-based actions. Delivery is triggered when the configured rule criteria are met; API reads provide supported resource data.
integrations.conditions: The workflow configuration determines which modules and changes produce notifications. Scheduled actions follow the chosen execution time. Reconciliation and other reads must respect the organization's API permissions and limits.

integrations.cadence: On configured automation events or scheduled API reads.
integrations.method: Odoo automation rules can send webhook notifications to external services. Its external API supports authorized record reads; synchronization timing depends on the installed version and deployment configuration.
integrations.conditions: Odoo Online external API access requires an eligible Custom plan. The enabled modules, automation triggers, hosting, and scheduled jobs determine timing. A self-hosted or customized deployment can have different capabilities.

integrations.cadence: Nightly for eligible connections; manual refresh when supported.
integrations.method: Flinks supports a daily scheduled refresh for eligible saved connections when scheduled refresh is enabled. Its published nightly job window is 04:00-08:00 UTC. An uncached authorization flow can request a manual refresh.
integrations.conditions: Eligibility depends on institution coverage, connection health, and applicable activity requirements. Some institutions do not support nightly refresh. MFA or credential changes can require the customer to reconnect; the nightly window is not a completion guarantee.

sources.title: Flinks nightly refresh requirements and routine

integrations.cadence: Typically 1-4 transaction updates per day.
integrations.method: Plaid typically checks transactions 1-4 times daily, depending on the institution. The `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` webhook signals changes that can be retrieved with `/transactions/sync`.
integrations.conditions: On-demand `/transactions/refresh` requires the separately enabled add-on and supported accounts. Reading cached data does not refresh the bank connection. Timing varies by institution and connection health.

integrations.cadence: Typically 1-4 transaction updates per day.
integrations.method: Plaid typically checks transactions 1-4 times daily, depending on the institution. The `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` webhook signals changes that can be retrieved with `/transactions/sync`.
integrations.conditions: On-demand `/transactions/refresh` requires the separately enabled add-on and supported accounts. Reading cached data does not refresh the bank connection. Timing varies by institution and connection health.

integrations.cadence: Daily subscribed transaction refresh; eligible on-demand requests.
integrations.method: Stripe Financial Connections refreshes transactions daily while an eligible active account is subscribed. A completion event reports the refresh result, after which transactions can be retrieved.
integrations.conditions: On-demand transaction refreshes must respect `transaction_refresh.next_refresh_available_at`. Inactive accounts cannot refresh. This daily cadence applies to subscribed transactions; balance and ownership are separate refresh features.

integrations.cadence: Approximately every 24 hours when background aggregation is enabled.
integrations.method: MX normally performs background aggregation about every 24 hours for eligible members. The source must allow it, and connection state and recent aggregation history affect eligibility.
integrations.conditions: Foreground aggregation requires the end user to be present. MX does not permit a new aggregation within three hours of a successful one. Disabled users, suspended connections, MFA, and institution restrictions can prevent refreshes.

integrations.cadence: Once daily for active accounts; restricted on-demand refresh.
integrations.method: Finicity automatically refreshes active accounts once per day. Its Refresh Customer Accounts endpoint allows a customer-specific refresh for a concrete business need, subject to product access.
integrations.conditions: The documented service prohibits automating calls to its Refresh endpoints. Additional refresh use must be agreed with the provider; repeated API reads do not force a new institution refresh. Availability also depends on the billing tier.

sources.title: Mastercard official Refresh Customer Accounts reference

integrations.cadence: Deployment-specific; agreed with the institution.
integrations.method: nCino exposes product-specific APIs across its platform. The lender's installed product, permitted objects, and integration configuration determine whether the connection uses supported notifications, scheduled reads, or an initiated workflow.
integrations.conditions: The public developer portal does not establish one refresh interval across all nCino products. Confirm the applicable API, event support, and approved schedule during onboarding; a mortgage-product capability must not be assumed for a business-banking deployment.

integrations.cadence: Workflow-specific; agreed for the connected decision flow.
integrations.method: The refresh arrangement follows the institution's Taktile decision-flow integration and the freshness of its inputs. Confirm the supported invocation, result-delivery method, and repeat-execution schedule for the connected flow.
integrations.conditions: Detailed API documentation requires customer access. The public reference does not establish a universal polling or refresh interval. A new decision execution does not by itself guarantee that an upstream financial-data source has refreshed.
